level: standalone Linux directory-descriptor-pinned brand-new file creation
componentAcceptance: verified within the stated standalone scope
productAcceptance: partial; not wired into Agent at this checkpoint

failures: The result observed nlink=2 before the private temp name was retired instead of the final one-link state.
Two symlinked-directory cases returned TARGET_PARENT_INVALID because Linux used ENOTDIR for O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW rather than ELOOP.

windowsGuard.note: Only the unsupported-platform case ran. The26 Linux cases are explicit skips, not Windows evidence.

observed: The published result is constructed after the private temp name is retired and the directory is synced; the returned and on-disk link count is one.
The published name must remain the same regular inode with exact size/mode and one link, and the payload is read back through the held file descriptor and compared byte for byte.
ENOTDIR is classified by lstat of the refused component, so a symlink is rejected as WORKSPACE_OUTSIDE_SCOPE without following it; a genuine non-directory remains TARGET_PARENT_INVALID.
Existing targets, directories, symlinks, dangling links and hard links to protected files are never overwritten. Concurrent target creation is refused and foreign links are not removed.

Parent replacement and relocation are detected around publication; cancellation before publication cleans the private name, while post-publish refusal carries possiblyApplied:true rather than false success.
limitations: This is a standalone component and is not yet product fs_write integration. Agent/Host admission, stop-receipt and root-pin compatibility require separate evidence.
Descriptor pinning binds an inode, not a path, mount, security label or external-writer CAS. The component deliberately refuses every existing target instead of overwriting.

The link() call still uses /proc/fd path strings because Node exposes no linkat(dirfd) API. Host-path checks bound and observe the remaining window but do not make it a kernel openat2/renameat2 proof.
Permissions/config generations, crash recovery of every publication point, Windows handle-relative creation and complete command/Task acceptance remain open.
